description: This RAND report, published on 30 September 2020, examines how Hurricanes Irma and Maria in 2017 damaged Puerto Rico's water sector and sets out a framework for recovery and transformation. Damage spread across drinking water, wastewater, stormwater and flood control infrastructure and water resources. RAND attributes it to three causes: the pre-existing vulnerability of the infrastructure, direct hurricane damage, and indirect disruption from other sectors, above all the loss of electrical power. The recovery plan involves repairing hurricane-damaged structures and fixing legacy challenges in infrastructure, operations and governance. Authors from RAND's Pardee and Homeland Security research units prepared it, with a research summary and downloadable PDF. Coverage: the island of Puerto Rico, 2017 to 2020. Access: free download from the RAND page; RAND permits sharing under its own terms, which were not read in full. Caveats: this is a planning-oriented assessment and not a dataset; some figures depend on utility and agency reports of varying date. It supports interdependency and recovery-planning models linking power and water, and relates to the catalogue's Puerto Rico electricity restoration and health services recovery case studies.
